text:
kjohnson: Heads-up — we need to size Dedicated pools for the new xlarge-62B bring-up. Two regions: us-west and eu-west. Questions: GPU mix (A100-80 vs H100), concurrency targets per GPU, and how much autoscale headroom to reserve for spikes. Any bench data or rough rules of thumb?

sara: I ran throughput/latency sweeps this morning on a 62B float16 / q4_khz model. Quick notes: A100-80: p50 token latency ~12ms, p95 ~38ms at concurrency 8; H100: p50 ~8ms, p95 ~25ms at concurrency 12. Throughput per GPU (tokens/sec) about 1.2x on H100.

sara: Also saw kernel variance: flash-attn v2 gives best tail latency for long contexts, but for short 2k contexts cuBLAS path had slightly more stable p95 on A100.
yuval: Important: quantization to q4_khz drops memory footprint ~30% and lets you bump concurrency. We tested q4_k on A100 -> safe to go concurrency 16 for typical 2k seq. For 8k seq we capped at 6 for p95 budget.
neil: For Dedicated sizing I'd propose baseline per-GPU concurrency targets: A100-80: 12 concurrent requests (2k avg), H100: 18 concurrent. Then reserve 30% headroom as warm reserve to avoid cold autoscale. That maps to: if you want 2000 qps-equivalent, plan GPUs = ceil(2000 / (qps_per_gpu * 0.7)).

kjohnson: Can you share example math / config? Ops team wants a template to plug numbers in.
sara: Sure — rough numbers from bench (2k avg, q4_k):
```
A100-80: tokens/sec ~= 35k -> approx 14 reqs/sec @ 2k tokens/request
H100: tokens/sec ~= 45k -> approx 20 reqs/sec @ 2k tokens/request
```
so for 100 reqs/s target: A100 gpus = ceil(100 / (14*0.7)) = ceil(100/9.8)=11, H100 gpus = ceil(100 / (20*0.7)) = ceil(100/14)=8.

yuval: Additions: account for prefix cache hit rate. If we expect 15% cache hits we can reduce GPUs by ~10% because those requests are ~5-10x cheaper. But don't count cache until we have traffic profile.
neil: Autoscale policy example we use in Dedicated:
```
policy:
  metric: requests_per_second
  target: 14 # per A100 GPU (2k avg)
  scale_up: 2 # add 2 GPUs on breach
  scale_down: 1
  cooldown: 120s
  reserved_capacity: 30% # warm spare
```
(For H100 target=20 instead).

kjohnson: How about multi-region routing? We may want to route burst traffic to eu-west if us-west saturates. Does cross-region fallback increase p95 too much?
sara: Yes, cross-region adds 40-120ms network tail depending on path. For p95-sensitive customers we should prefer keeping them local. For best-effort workloads redirecting to eu-west is fine. We tested fallback: local p95 30ms -> remote p95 170ms.
yuval: Kernel selection: default to flash-attn for H100; A100 use autoselect but prefer cuBLAS for <=2k avg if p95 is the priority. We'll bake that into model variant metadata so routing can pick variant with appropriate kernel flags.
neil: Ops note — Dedicated billing/commitments: if we plan for 30% reserved, we can map reserved nodes to cheaper reserved contracts and use burst pool (preemptible) for the rest. That combo drops effective cost ~18%.

kjohnson: Any open risks?
sara: Regression risk from quant configs. We need evals on production prompts before enabling q4_k by default. Quick sanity: run N=500 prompt eval; check rouge/accuracy thresholds.
yuval: Also watch for KV cache memory blowups at 8k tokens on q4_khz on A100 — need a guard that rejects requests > max_cached_len when concurrency is high.
neil: I'll draft a Dedicated sizing template and autoscale snippet and drop in #eng-platform ops playbook. ETA end of day. :rocket:

infra-bot: deploy/cluster-sim v2 ran at 1769990300: simulated 2k req/s profile for us-west A100 pool -> suggested 12 gpus with 30% reserved headroom (matches sara/neil calc).

kjohnson: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll coordinate with sales on SLA tiers & put a canary plan for eu-west failover. :thumbsup:
